impact: A wrong floor written into scripts/verify-baselines.env, derived by the exact command the file tells you to use. BASELINE_ROOT_FULL_TESTS is the one number verify.sh cannot print a MEASURED block for (its stage fails on this box for want of /home/ubuntu fixtures), so it has ALWAYS been hand-derived with this command -- every prior revision's recorded provenance used it. The gate itself was never at risk: verify.sh gates on awk (verify.sh:179). Root cause: this agent harness shims grep to ugrep 7.5.0, whose -o emitted 526 of 527 matching lines on a 9279-line log, dropping one '2 passed'. grep -c and grep -n both matched all 527 on the same file, so nothing looked wrong. Deterministic across three consecutive runs, and it also reproduces without \\K, so it is ugrep's -o generally rather than the lookbehind.
resolution: Fixed at source rather than worked around: scripts/verify-baselines.env now carries a COUNTING A LOG BY HAND section prescribing the awk form -- byte-for-byte verify.sh's own sum_passed counter -- and requiring a third implementation as cross-check before any floor moves. The floors written this run (5825/526) were confirmed by awk, GNU grep 3.11 via 'command grep', and a python re-parse, all three agreeing on both runs' logs.
summary: the re-measurement command verify-baselines.env prescribes (grep -oP ... | paste -sd+ | bc) silently under-reports by 2 under a ugrep-shimmed grep; awk/GNU grep/python all agree on 5825
